### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c1240a38ac2c23c8d526e476a20edeabbbefd6f6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4e0943281d97d0993a2f89f8a35ad5f6f978674c` — the merge of head `41db2e116df54c05dfb38be4cfc0a0d5d58a5a24` into base `c1240a38ac2c23c8d526e476a20edeabbbefd6f6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4e0943281d97d0993a2f89f8a35ad5f6f978674c && git checkout 4e0943281d97d0993a2f89f8a35ad5f6f978674c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c1240a38ac2c23c8d526e476a20edeabbbefd6f6 41db2e116df54c05dfb38be4cfc0a0d5d58a5a24 && git checkout -B drift-repro c1240a38ac2c23c8d526e476a20edeabbbefd6f6 && git merge --no-ff 41db2e116df54c05dfb38be4cfc0a0d5d58a5a24

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c1240a38ac2c23c8d526e476a20edeabbbefd6f6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `12fb7d30196dbf2dff1ab4858157efc266b30005`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-failed-read.pin.test.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json, packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json, .changeset/30251-ownership-queue-on-failed-read.md (the whole diff against merge-base `959c26be`, one commit, +158/−3); at `origin/main`: docs/adr/0142 (status line, D2 as amended, D6 and D7 notes), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts (the one implementer), ownership-queue.test.ts, position-graph.ts, business-unit-graph.ts, packages/spec/tsconfig.test.json, package.json, test-typecheck-debt.json, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, .github/workflows/lint.yml; card #30251 (body, comments 6649330330, 6649914605, 6649969637, 6650955285), #29604 comments 6648911579 and 6600766777, contract review 6600699486 on PR #29865, PR #30318 body and comments 6650956931, 6650966285; the 41 check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

- Pure widening, verified at the type level and by census. `expandMembers` keeps `options?` and adds one optional key (`ownership-queue-service.ts:139-143`); `isMember` gains a fourth, optional, trailing argument (`:155-160`). Every caller at `origin/main` reaches the service through a `Pick` and calls with no options, `{}`-equivalent or `{ purpose: 'addressing' }` (`approval-service.ts:3347`, `assignment-rules.ts:293`, `sharing-rule-service.ts:1747, :2186`, `sharing-service.ts:952`, `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:1602`, `security-plugin-explain-access.ts:512`, `kernel-queue-membership.test.ts:113`, `ownership-queue.test.ts`); the PR's census table matches my grep hit for hit, and the remaining hits use only `OWNERSHIP_QUEUE_SERVICE` or `hasAnyQueue`/`queuesOf`/`declaredQueueNamed`, members the diff does not touch. The one implementer (`plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts:171-186`) declares `{ purpose? }` and a three-parameter `isMember`; it stays assignable (fewer trailing parameters, and `{ purpose?; onFailedRead? }` is assignable to `{ purpose? }`), which the pin's `legacy` object proves at compile time (`pin.test.ts:52-57`). Omitting the key is today's answer: the default is `'nobody'` and nothing at runtime changed.
- The silent-ignore case is real and the docblock does not name it. The implementer at main consults neither key: `expandMembers` builds `newPass(options?.purpose)` only (`:178`) and `isMember` takes no options (`:181`), so a caller passing `{ onFailedRead: 'refuse' }` against the registered service today gets `'nobody'`, logged once at `warn` (`expandSpec` `:309-314`, `holderCheck` `:394-403`, `warnOnce` `:541`). The contract's `'refuse'` bullet (`:69-73`) states the rejection as a promise with no clause on who honours it or from when; only the PR body, the changeset and the module header's "What the expander answers then is the caller's to say" carry the split. Route A (6648911579) ruled the split and the card says no runtime change, so this is not a false claim about the design, but the published docblock is the text a third-package caller reads — should-fix 1.
- The pin is not a phantom: `tsconfig.test.json` includes `src/**/*`, `check:test-typecheck` is in spec's `typecheck` script (`package.json:320, :323`), which `Type Check · workspace` runs through `turbo run typecheck` (`lint.yml:5665, :5681`); the new file has no debt entry, so zero errors is the ratchet. No shared harness exists for this contract in spec (`queue-service.test.ts` is the JOB queue's `IQueueService`), so a new file is right under ruling 6583487846.
- Docblock against D2 as amended: both answers, the D3/D4/D5-nobody and D6/D7-refuse split, "logged at `warn`", a refusal that names the read and is never `[]`/partial/`false`, an empty queue and a name that resolves nowhere still `[]`/`false` — each matches D2's text and the D6/D7 notes. The table list is true of the code at main: `sys_queue` (`authoredQueueRow`), `sys_queue_member` (`authoredMemberSpecs`), `sys_team_member` (`TeamGraphService`), `sys_user_position` plus `sys_member` through `expandRoleUsers`/`holdsRole` (`position-graph.ts:119, :167`, the limb 6600766777 asked the code half to treat as a failed read), and the BU membership and tree (`BusinessUnitGraphService`, `sys_business_unit_member` and `sys_business_unit`, `business-unit-graph.ts:46-47`), reached through `expandSpecUncached` `:331-341`. D2 names `sys_business_unit_member` and the BU tree itself, so the dev's addition beyond the card's list is D2's, not an invention. Nothing in the `'nobody'` bullet is future work; the `'refuse'` bullet is the future-work gap above.
- Check-runs on `12fb7d30`: 41; at reading time 15 success, 8 skipped by path filter, 18 in progress, 0 failure. Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Spec property liveness and Dogfood Regression Gate are success; the Type Check lanes (the one that compiles the pin) and Test Core shards were still running. No governed path in the file list.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec: patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none`: `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` grades every entry under `none` as `patch` (header lines 12-13, 909-910), and the level lost its coupling to `Clause-②` (901-918), so `patch` on a widening of a published type is the reading, not a downgrade. Check Changeset is success on the head.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)`: `readArmToken` matches `(widening` followed by a non-word character, so the colon reads as the `widening` arm, not a near miss (`clause2-line.mjs:311-313`). `Metadata-protocol: none` is right — no key, value or metadata type an author writes moves. ADR-0087 is not needed: nothing is removed, renamed, aliased or tombstoned.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Should-fix 1 — the `'refuse'` bullet (`ownership-queue-service.ts:69-73`) promises a rejection the registered implementation does not yet make. One clause: an implementation written before the key answers `'nobody'`; the platform producer in `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` honours `'refuse'` from #29604's code half. The PR body and changeset say it; the published docblock, which is what a caller outside plugin-sharing reads, does not.
- Should-fix 2 — the sentence "The tables behind a queue are …" (`:57-62`) reads as exhaustive and omits the activation ledger (`sys_metadata_activation`), a read the expansion makes (`switchedOff` at `:247, :416`; `positionActive` at `:334, :371`) whose failure is answered "on", not nobody — a posture neither value describes. 6600766777 leaves it to the code half to decide and say; with the contract silent, #29604 must reopen this spec file to say it. One clause either way ("the activation ledger read keeps its regime-C posture and is not a failed read in this sense", or that it is one) closes the loop here. Wording in the same sentence: the BU entries are named by role while every other entry is a table name; D2 names `sys_business_unit_member`.
- Not findings: `_ExpandOptionKeys` pins the exact key set, so a future option reds this pin by design; `queuesOf` takes no key, and no ADR-0142 recompute consumer reads it; `isMember`'s `purpose` is refused by the excess-property check, as the pin shows.

### ④ Design judgment

The signal is the one D2 says the consumer sends, spelled once as an exported value type both methods read, trailing and optional on both, and kept off the `purpose` axis in the type, the docblock (`:79-81`) and the pin (`_AxesDisjoint`, the `'addressing'` and `purpose`-on-`isMember` refusals) — exactly what review 6600699486 required and route A chose. The pins would fail without the change: the type import, the `Eq` on `isMember`'s fourth parameter and the `{ onFailedRead: 'refuse' }` calls do not compile against main's contract. Body matches code: `Fixes #30251`, `Part of #29604`, the census, `Prior rulings read:` and the 维护者速读 are present and accurate; the generated `api-surface` and `export-origins` carry the one new export and nothing else moves (no ADR anchor names this file, no `skills/**` or `content/docs/**` page names any method).
